"In the Green" is down to four top prizes after a $50,000 winner was claimed over a week ago. The game started with seven top prizes. Know that before you buy, because a change in top prizes changes the whole game.

The numbers for "In the Green" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
810.headline: A player won a top prize

811.body:
The top prize count on "Extreme Green" has not moved for close to two months. The game still has four of five top prizes unclaimed. Smaller prizes keep getting claimed as tickets sell. The same top prizes are now among fewer tickets.

For "Extreme Green" or any game, being late in a run is not automatically good or bad. The same numbers mean different things near the end of a run.

Everything above about "Extreme Green" comes from the Maryland Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
811.headline: Tickets sell, top prizes remain

812.body:
"Loose Change®" is near the midpoint of its run, with about two-thirds of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, the top prizes and the tickets are going at about the same pace.

Tomorrow's count on "Loose Change®" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.

If "The Price is Right™" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
